references.text: God promises Abraham that Sarah will bear a son named Isaac, and that He will establish His covenant with him. Isaac's growth and weaning celebration confirm that this promise has been fulfilled.
The Lord's message that Sarah will bear a son within the next year, leading to Isaac's birth and the subsequent celebration at his weaning.
The immediate context describing Isaac's birth and how God fulfilled His promise to Abraham and Sarah, with Sarah's joy and laughter.
Hebrews refers to Abraham's and Sarah's faith in God's promise of descendants despite their old age—a faith rewarded by Isaac's birth and growth.
Hannah weans Samuel and brings him to the house of the Lord—a parallel to Isaac's weaning feast, where weaning marks an important milestone in the child's life.
